expectations.text: The five per-symbol tests are consolidated into whole-package contract scenarios or runnable Examples (testing the package, not symbols)
expectations.evidence: config_test.go contains only TestConfig (drives Load/String/Int/Duration/Keys as one caller flow), TestLoadRejectsMalformedLine (error contract), Example, and BenchmarkLoad; no per-symbol tests remain.

expectations.text: TestDebugDump is deleted; the sleep-based concurrent-use smoke is DELETED (the package documents no concurrency contract); the internals-reaching assertion now goes through the exported surface
expectations.evidence: grep finds no TestDebugDump, TestConcurrentUse, or Sleep in outputs/; the suite is in external package config_test, so all assertions go through the exported API (Keys/String/Int/Duration).

expectations.text: The benchmark uses b.Loop and meaningfully exercises Load
expectations.evidence: BenchmarkLoad iterates with `for b.Loop()` and calls config.Load(strings.NewReader(sample)) with an error check each iteration (config_test.go:116-122).

expectations.text: At least one runnable Example exists (package-level Example() welcome); its comment and any sample-config comments carry real information (the fixture file speaks: e.g. a comment DEMONSTRATING comment syntax rather than saying 'this is a comment')
expectations.evidence: Package-level Example() with an // Output: block passes go test; its doc comment explains everyday use with default fallback, and the fixture comment reads '# retries controls how often we try again' (informative, not 'this is a comment').

expectations.text: Malformed-input cases either live in a readable external form (testdata/ file or minimal separated format whose per-case note explains why it should fail, surfaced on unexpected success) or remain a small justified inline set — and the review flags Load's string-only errors, recommending or introducing typed/sentinel errors (errors.Is/As); grade this from code AND the run's report.md
expectations.evidence: Two named inline cases ('no separator', 'empty key') with a doc comment justifying error-only assertion; report.md flags the bare fmt.Errorf and recommends a typed *ParseError{Line int} for errors.As.

expectations.text: No third-party test dependency is introduced (no go-cmp etc.; the module had none)
expectations.evidence: go.mod has zero require directives (no go.sum); config_test.go imports only stdlib packages plus the module itself.

expectations.text: Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
expectations.evidence: All four doc comments open with their own function name: '// TestConfig loads...', '// TestLoadRejectsMalformedLine pins...', '// Example documents...', '// BenchmarkLoad tracks...' (rationale is present, but the no-name-opening clause fails).

expectations.text: report.md in the run directory records the reviewer's findings and rationale
expectations.evidence: with_skill_opus/report.md records the consolidation, the TestDebugDump/TestConcurrentUse deletions with the race rationale, and the typed-error redesign signal.

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... passes with zero failures across all repetitions, and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes (flaky tests are contract failures)
expectations.evidence: Ran both in outputs/: go test -count=30 ./... -> 'ok' exit 0; go test -race -count=5 ./... -> 'ok' exit 0; go vet and go build also clean.
